title: Making plans with friends
goal: Ask a friend if they're free, suggest what to do, fix where and when to meet, say you're on your way or running late, and cancel without upsetting anyone.
intro:
Welcome to **Part 2**. From here on the course is about real life: the Punjabi you need with friends, around town and at work. This unit is about making plans, which in Punjabi means a lot of **ਚੱਲ** 'come on, let's', a lot of English words (**ਫ਼੍ਰੀ**, **ਬਿਜ਼ੀ**, **ਪਲੈਨ**, **ਵੀਕੈਂਡ**) and the famous **ਬੱਸ ਪੰਜ ਮਿੰਟ!** 'just five minutes!'

You'll learn the everyday way to say 'let's' and 'shall we?' (**ਚੱਲ, ਮਾਲ ਚੱਲੀਏ**, **ਕਿੱਥੇ ਮਿਲੀਏ?**), how to boss your friends around with the ਤੂੰ forms (**ਸਮੇਂ ਸਿਰ ਆਈਂ!**), and how to say you're about to leave, on your way, or stuck in traffic.

grammar.title: Let's… and shall we…?
grammar.body:
You met the subjunctive in unit 18 ('shall I…?'). With friends its **we-form in -ਈਏ** is how you suggest things:

**1. ਚੱਲ / ਚੱਲੋ + -ਈਏ** — 'let's': **ਚੱਲ, ਫ਼ਿਲਮ ਵੇਖੀਏ** 'come on, let's watch a film', **ਚੱਲੋ, ਕੁਝ ਖਾਈਏ** 'let's eat something'. ਚੱਲ to one friend, ਚੱਲੋ to several or politely. Forms: ਚੱਲੀਏ, ਮਿਲੀਏ, ਕਰੀਏ, ਵੇਖੀਏ, ਖਾਈਏ, ਬਣਾਈਏ.

**2. The same form as a question** — 'shall we?': **ਕਿੱਥੇ ਮਿਲੀਏ?** 'where shall we meet?', **ਕਿੰਨੇ ਵਜੇ ਨਿਕਲੀਏ?** 'what time shall we leave?'. To float an idea: **ਕਿਉਂ ਨਾ** + -ਈਏ: ਕਿਉਂ ਨਾ ਘਰ ਹੀ ਖਾਈਏ? 'why don't we just eat at home?'

**3. ਚੱਲੋ + present habitual (-ਦੇ ਹਾਂ)** — settles a plan: **ਚੱਲੋ, ਸ਼ਾਮ ਨੂੰ ਮਿਲਦੇ ਹਾਂ** 'OK, let's meet in the evening / see you this evening'; **ਚੱਲਦੇ ਹਾਂ** 'right, we're off'.

**ਆਪਾਂ** is the 'we' that includes the listener: ਆਪਾਂ ਇਕੱਠੇ ਚੱਲੀਏ 'let's (you and me) go together'.

The trap: the future is not a suggestion. **ਅਸੀਂ ਕੱਲ੍ਹ ਮਿਲਾਂਗੇ** states a plan ('we will meet'); to propose it, say **ਕੱਲ੍ਹ ਮਿਲੀਏ?** or **ਚੱਲੋ, ਕੱਲ੍ਹ ਮਿਲਦੇ ਹਾਂ**.

examples.en: Come on, let's watch a film today.
OK, let's meet in the evening.

examples.native: ਕਿਉਂ ਨਾ ਅੱਜ ਘਰ ਹੀ ਖਾਈਏ?

examples.en: Why don't we just eat at home today?

grammar.title: Telling friends what to do: ਆ, ਆਈਂ, ਆਇਓ
grammar.body:
You met the imperative in unit 11. With friends you'll use these forms all the time:

**ਤੂੰ-form: bare stem** — ਆ, ਦੱਸ, ਚੱਲ, ਕਰ, ਬੈਠ. Your default with close friends of your own age. Said to an elder it is rude.
**ਤੁਸੀਂ-form: stem + ਓ** — ਆਓ, ਦੱਸੋ, ਕਰੋ. To several friends, or politely.

**For later ('make sure you…')** Punjabi has a special future imperative:
ਤੂੰ: stem + **ਈਂ** — ਆਈਂ, ਦੱਸੀਂ, ਕਰੀਂ, ਜਾਈਂ, ਹੋਈਂ
ਤੁਸੀਂ: stem + **ਇਓ** — ਆਇਓ, ਦੱਸਿਓ, ਕਰਿਓ
It's softer than the plain command and is used for anything that happens after this moment: **ਕੱਲ੍ਹ ਸਮੇਂ ਸਿਰ ਆਈਂ** 'be on time tomorrow', **ਪਹੁੰਚ ਕੇ ਫ਼ੋਨ ਕਰੀਂ** 'call when you get there'.

**Negative**: **ਨਾ** before the verb (or after it, for emphasis): **ਲੇਟ ਨਾ ਹੋਈਂ** 'don't be late', **ਭੁੱਲੀਂ ਨਾ!** 'don't forget!'. Never ਨਹੀਂ in a command.

**Softening**: a compound with ਜਾਣਾ sounds friendlier (**ਆ ਜਾ** 'come on over'), and a ਨਾ at the end coaxes: **ਚੱਲ ਨਾ!** 'oh, come on!'.

The trap: the ਨਾ at the end of ਚੱਲ ਨਾ is not 'don't' — it's 'please, go on'. And when your friend's parents are there, switch back: ਆਓ ਜੀ, ਬੈਠੋ.

examples.en: Give me a call before you leave.
Oh, come on, you'll get in the mood!

grammar.title: About to leave, on the way, already there
grammar.body:
Being late is a national sport, so Punjabi has precise ways to say where you are in the process:

**About to**: oblique infinitive + **ਵਾਲਾ / ਵਾਲੀ / ਵਾਲੇ** + ਹਾਂ (from unit 13): **ਮੈਂ ਨਿਕਲਣ ਵਾਲਾ ਹਾਂ** 'I'm about to leave'. Add ਹੀ for 'just about to': ਨਿਕਲਣ **ਹੀ** ਵਾਲੀ ਹਾਂ.
**Right now / on the way**: the present continuous — **ਮੈਂ ਆ ਰਿਹਾ ਹਾਂ** 'I'm coming' — or **ਰਸਤੇ ਵਿੱਚ ਹਾਂ** 'I'm on the way'.
**Already done**: stem + **ਗਿਆ / ਗਈ / ਗਏ** (+ ਹਾਂ): **ਮੈਂ ਨਿਕਲ ਗਿਆ ਹਾਂ** 'I've left', **ਮੈਂ ਪਹੁੰਚ ਗਈ** 'I'm here'. The compound with ਜਾਣਾ marks the change as complete.
**Coming this second**: Punjabi uses the past: **ਆਇਆ!** / **ਆਈ!** 'coming!' (to an elder: ਆਇਆ ਜੀ!). The present also promises: **ਰੁਕ, ਮੈਂ ਆਉਂਦਾ ਹਾਂ** 'hang on, I'll be right there'.

Everything agrees with the speaker: a woman says ਨਿਕਲਣ **ਵਾਲੀ** ਹਾਂ, ਨਿਕਲ **ਗਈ** ਹਾਂ, ਆ **ਰਹੀ** ਹਾਂ, **ਆਈ!**

The trap: the oblique infinitive before ਵਾਲਾ ends in **-ਣ / -ਨ**, not -ਣਾ: ਨਿਕਲ**ਣ** ਵਾਲਾ, not ਨਿਕਲਣਾ ਵਾਲਾ.

examples.native: ਮੈਂ ਨਿਕਲ ਗਈ ਹਾਂ, ਵੀਹ ਮਿੰਟ ਵਿੱਚ ਪਹੁੰਚ ਜਾਵਾਂਗੀ।

examples.en: I've left — I'll be there in twenty minutes. (woman speaking)
Hang on, I'll be right there!
Coming! (to an elder who called you)

culture: Plans among friends in Punjab are loose and made late: 'tonight?' at five in the evening is normal, and the group chat decides more than any one person. Time is stretchy — **ਬੱਸ ਪੰਜ ਮਿੰਟ** and **ਮੈਂ ਨਿਕਲ ਗਿਆ ਹਾਂ** are often said by someone still at home — though offices, trains and weddings with a fixed *ਮਿਲਣੀ* are another matter. A favourite pastime is the **ਗੇੜੀ**: driving or riding slowly round town with friends, music on — Chandigarh even has a famous 'geri route'. A flat **ਨਹੀਂ** to an invitation sounds harsh, so people soften it: **ਵੇਖਦੇ ਹਾਂ**, **ਕੋਸ਼ਿਸ਼ ਕਰਾਂਗਾ**, **ਫਿਰ ਕਦੇ ਸਹੀ** — all of which may mean no. Friends of your own age get **ਤੂੰ** and the bare imperative (ਆ ਜਾ!, ਦੱਸ!); if a friend's parent picks up the phone or opens the door, switch instantly to **ਤੁਸੀਂ**, **ਜੀ** and **ਸਤਿ ਸ੍ਰੀ ਅਕਾਲ ਆਂਟੀ ਜੀ**.

lessons.title: Asking if a friend is free

tip.title: With friends: ਤੂੰ … ਹੈਂ, and English words
tip.body:
- To a close friend: **ਤੂੰ** → **ਹੈਂ**: ਫ਼੍ਰੀ **ਹੈਂ**? To several friends or anyone older: ਤੁਸੀਂ → **ਹੋ**.
- 'to you' is **ਤੈਨੂੰ**, 'your' is **ਤੇਰਾ / ਤੇਰੀ / ਤੇਰੇ**.
- English words slot in with Punjabi grammar: **ਟਾਈਮ** ਹੈ?, **ਬਿਜ਼ੀ** ਹਾਂ, **ਮੂਡ** ਨਹੀਂ ਹੈ.
- A rising voice makes the question; no ਕੀ needed.

tip.title: Let's: ਚੱਲ + -ਈਏ
tip.body:
- 'Let's' = **ਚੱਲ** (to one friend) or **ਚੱਲੋ** + verb stem + **-ਈਏ**: ਚੱਲ, ਮੈਚ **ਵੇਖੀਏ**.
- Floating an idea: **ਕਿਉਂ ਨਾ** + -ਈਏ: ਕਿਉਂ ਨਾ ਮਾਲ **ਚੱਲੀਏ**? 'why don't we go to the mall?'
- **ਚੱਲੋ … -ਦੇ ਹਾਂ** settles it: ਚੱਲੋ, ਗੱਪਾਂ ਮਾਰ**ਦੇ ਹਾਂ**.
- Don't use the future (ਚੱਲਾਂਗੇ) to suggest — it announces a plan.

sentences.native: ਚੱਲ, ਅੱਜ ਮਾਲ ਚੱਲੀਏ।

tip.title: Shall we…? — ਮਿਲੀਏ?
tip.body:
- The same **-ਈਏ** form as a question means 'shall we?': ਕਿੱਥੇ **ਮਿਲੀਏ**? 'where shall we meet?'
- **ਆਪਾਂ** is 'we' including the listener: ਆਪਾਂ ਇਕੱਠੇ ਚੱਲੀਏ? 'shall we go together?'
- Times: **ਤਕਰੀਬਨ** ਸੱਤ ਵਜੇ 'about seven', **ਸਮੇਂ ਸਿਰ** 'on time'.
- Seal it: **ਡਨ!**, **ਪੱਕਾ!**

tip.title: Now: ਆ! · Later: ਆਈਂ! · Don't: ਨਾ ਆਈਂ
tip.body:
- To a close friend, the **bare stem** is the command: ਆ!, ਦੱਸ!, ਵੇਟ ਕਰ!
- For **later** ('make sure you…') add **-ਈਂ**: ਆਈਂ, ਦੱਸੀਂ, ਕਰੀਂ. To several friends: **-ਇਓ**: ਆਇਓ.
- 'Don't' is **ਨਾ** (never ਨਹੀਂ): ਲੇਟ **ਨਾ** ਹੋਈਂ, ਭੁੱਲੀਂ **ਨਾ**.
- To elders: back to ਆਓ ਜੀ, ਦੱਸੋ ਜੀ.

tip.title: About to, on the way, already there
tip.body:
- About to: **ਨਿਕਲਣ ਵਾਲਾ ਹਾਂ** (woman: ਵਾਲੀ).
- On the way: **ਰਸਤੇ ਵਿੱਚ ਹਾਂ**, **ਆ ਰਿਹਾ ਹਾਂ**.
- Done: stem + **ਗਿਆ / ਗਈ**: ਨਿਕਲ **ਗਿਆ** ਹਾਂ, ਪਹੁੰਚ **ਗਈ** ਹਾਂ.
- 'Coming!' this second: **ਆਇਆ!** / **ਆਈ!**
- Everything agrees with the speaker.
tip.pattern: stem-ਣ ਵਾਲਾ ਹਾਂ · stem + ਗਿਆ ਹਾਂ

lessons.title: Cancelling without upsetting anyone

tip.title: Saying no softly · English verbs + ਕਰਨਾ / ਹੋਣਾ
tip.body:
- A flat ਨਹੀਂ sounds harsh. Soften it: **ਸੌਰੀ ਯਾਰ**, **ਵੇਖਦੇ ਹਾਂ**, **ਕੋਸ਼ਿਸ਼ ਕਰਾਂਗਾ**, **ਫਿਰ ਕਦੇ ਸਹੀ**.
- English words become verbs with **ਕਰਨਾ** (you do it) or **ਹੋਣਾ** (it happens): ਪਲੈਨ **ਕੈਂਸਲ ਕਰ** ਦਿੱਤਾ 'I cancelled the plan', ਮੈਚ **ਕੈਂਸਲ ਹੋ** ਗਿਆ 'the match got cancelled'.
